title: Dolly Parton
overview: Dolly Rebecca Parton (January 19, 1946 – August 25, 2026) — the Queen of Country, a songwriter’s songwriter, and East Tennessee’s most famous ambassador. These are the 25 answers a good pub quiz reaches for first.
spoilerNote: Facts favored for general-knowledge and music rounds — not deep-cut discography.

facts.fact: She was born Dolly Rebecca Parton on January 19, 1946, in a one-room cabin in Sevier County, Tennessee (Locust Ridge / near Pittman Center).
She was the fourth of twelve children born to Avie Lee and Robert Lee Parton.
The day after graduating from Sevier County High School in 1964, she moved to Nashville to chase a music career.
She married Carl Thomas Dean on May 30, 1966, in Ringgold, Georgia — they stayed married nearly 60 years until his death in 2025.
Her debut full-length album was Hello, I’m Dolly (1967).
Her big TV break was joining The Porter Wagoner Show in 1967, replacing Norma Jean.
Her first No. 1 country single was “Joshua” (1971).
“Coat of Many Colors” (1971) is about a coat her mother sewed from rags — kids at school mocked it, and she wore it with pride.
“Jolene” topped the country chart in 1974; she wrote it after a bank teller kept flirting with Carl Dean.
She wrote “I Will Always Love You” (1974) about leaving Porter Wagoner’s show — not about a romantic breakup.
Elvis Presley wanted to record “I Will Always Love You,” but she refused when Colonel Tom Parker demanded half the publishing.
Whitney Houston’s 1992 Bodyguard version of “I Will Always Love You” made Parton millions more in publishing than her own hit ever had.
“Here You Come Again” (1977) was her first million-selling album and first major pop crossover smash.
She starred with Jane Fonda and Lily Tomlin in the film 9 to 5 (1980) and wrote its Oscar-nominated title song.
“9 to 5” hit No. 1 on the country, pop, and adult-contemporary charts — a rare triple crown.
“Islands in the Stream,” her 1983 No. 1 duet with Kenny Rogers, was written by the Bee Gees.
Dollywood, her theme park in Pigeon Forge, Tennessee, opened in 1986 (on the former Silver Dollar City site).
She co-starred in Steel Magnolias (1989) with Julia Roberts, Sally Field, Shirley MacLaine, Olympia Dukakis, and Daryl Hannah.
She was inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame in 1999.
Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library (founded 1995) mails free books to children from birth to kindergarten — inspired by her father, who never learned to read.
She donated $1 million that helped fund early Moderna COVID-19 vaccine research at Vanderbilt — then got the shot herself and joked about a “dose of her own medicine.”
She initially declined a Rock & Roll Hall of Fame nomination (saying it was for rockers), then accepted and was inducted in 2022.
She is tied with Reba McEntire for the most Billboard No. 1 country singles by a woman (25).
She has written more than 3,000 songs and sold more than 100 million records worldwide.
On Disney Channel’s Hannah Montana, she played Aunt Dolly — godmother to real-life goddaughter Miley Cyrus.
